## DAG FEED-fk (2026-06-27): MUON-AS-SPECTRAL-CONDITIONER deep-math + topology verdict (LENS B of the 3-lens "bridge all levels and dimensions" review) — Muon conditions the ILL-CONDITIONED low-energy boundary-annulus subspace AdamW starves; the curriculum×codim×dimension lattice is COHERENT + largely orthogonal; Muon RESPECTS the R passband IFF on the realized-through-R loss + eikonal-held; Muon is the most-potent OPTIMIZER lever but the binding limit after it is the **Movable medial-axis REPRESENTATION** (a chart limit, not a conditioning limit), not the d_seg budget itself. (CPU-only $0 derivation+code-read; GPU UNTOUCHED pid 8806; pointer UNMOVED **0.19110**; NO-FAKE — everything below is a DERIVATION/PREDICTION grounded in Kronecker/K-FAC Hessian theory + the MEASURED "Muon is THE drop" + the NS-orthogonalization unit-tests, NOT a measured d_seg row on this witness; means≠ends — a math verdict moves nothing; SANDBOX/RULE-6)

**Surfaces read:** `src/tac/optimization/muon_finisher_mlx.py` (the param partition: 2-D `in_proj/film/hidden.*` → Muon; biases/1-D/`code`/`out_sdf`/`out_tex` → AdamW), `tac.optimization.md_decoupling.newton_schulz5` (the orthogonalizer, byte-faithful to MLX Muon: quintic 3.4445/−4.7750/2.0315, pre-normalize, transpose-for-wide), `src/tac/boundary_math/lever_b_levelset_generator.py` (the decoder: `code→film(code)→FiLM-MLP on curvelet/Fourier coord-feats through hosc tanh(β·sin(ω·u))→out_sdf→K φ_k→softmax→palette→RGB`; `eikonal_penalty` |∇φ|→1; margin `m=φ_top1−φ_top2`), FEED-fd/fe/ff/fg/fh/fi.

### (1) WHY Muon is "THE drop" — the eigenvalue picture (the mechanism, derived)
The per-layer loss Hessian of a linear map `W∈R^{m×n}` has the Gauss-Newton/K-FAC **Kronecker structure** `H ≈ A ⊗ G` (input-feature covariance ⊗ output-gradient covariance), so `κ(H) = κ(A)·κ(G)`. For THIS decoder the inputs are curvelet/Fourier coord-features and FiLM-modulated activations whose energy is overwhelmingly carried by the **80.2% static-core bulk** (FEED-fd) — a few high-energy directions dominate `A` and `G`, while the **codim-1 boundary-annulus directions (Lane+Movable, ~4.67% of px, FEED-dq)** are LOW-energy → tiny Hessian eigenvalues → severely ill-conditioned, with the small-eigenvalue subspace = exactly where d_seg lives.
- **AdamW = diagonal preconditioner** (`Δ ∝ g/√v`): it equalizes the per-coordinate gradient MAGNITUDE but is BLIND to the off-diagonal/spectral anisotropy of `A⊗G`. It moves fast along the bulk (large-eigenvalue) directions and CRAWLS along the low-energy boundary directions ⇒ the boundary annulus under-fits ⇒ **d_seg plateaus** (the measured 0.03/0.032 flat plateau, FEED-ew §977-979; and the generic "smooth RAISES, Muon is THE drop" ranking).
- **Muon = spectral/operator-norm preconditioner.** Newton-Schulz replaces the momentum-update `M = UΣVᵀ` by `≈UVᵀ` (Σ→I; the unit-tests confirm an 8×-spread spectrum collapses into the ~[0.68,1.13] band). Orthogonalizing the update = **whitening the step in the matrix/operator sense** = approximate steepest descent under the **spectral (2→2) norm** instead of Frobenius. Every singular direction of the weight-update gets a UNIT-norm step REGARDLESS of its gradient energy ⇒ the low-energy boundary directions get moved at the SAME rate as the bulk ⇒ the starved subspace is released. **Eigenvalue picture: AdamW equalizes diag(H); Muon equalizes the SINGULAR SPECTRUM of the per-layer update = equalizing the eigenvalues of H restricted to that layer in the Kronecker approx** → κ(update)→1 → the small-eigenvalue (boundary-placement) directions stop being starved. That is the mechanistic reason Muon is THE drop: the binding d_seg residual is precisely the ill-conditioned low-energy subspace, and Muon is the one optimizer in the stack that conditions it.
- **Does it condition the boundary annulus / separatrix specifically? YES, via PLACEMENT (not slope).** The capacity to PLACE the margin-zero set `m=φ_top1−φ_top2` precisely lives in `in_proj/hidden` (carving φ_k near the codim-1 boundary) and `film` (per-frame boundary motion). Orthogonalized updates let those low-energy directions refine the separatrix LOCATION → fewer of the ~244 px margin-gated flip-residual (FEED-fh). **Crucial complementarity:** Muon does NOT touch the field MAGNITUDE/slope |∇φ| (that is the eikonal's job, |∇φ|→1 ⇒ |∇m|~O(1) ⇒ 587× R-survival). So **eikonal fixes the boundary SLOPE (R-survival); Muon fixes the boundary PLACEMENT (d_seg accuracy)** — orthogonal actuators on orthogonal geometric quantities. This resolves a latent confusion: "sharper" through Muon is NOT field-sharpness (that would fight R); it is placement-precision in weight space.

### (2) BRIDGED LATTICE — curriculum × codim-strata × dimension (where each lever acts; coherence map)
Dimensions: **2D frame → 3D spacetime (the ~8-dim Lane manifold across n600, FEED-ew §591) → K-logit normal-fan** (argmax of 5 φ_k = an additively-weighted power diagram in R^5; its 1-skeleton = the Morse-Smale separatrix graph, FEED-fh AUC 0.9987). Codim strata: **codim-1 boundary** (Lane+Movable annulus) · **codim-2 triple points** (3 classes tie) · **codim-3 quad / birth-death** (4 classes tie; a class appears/vanishes).

| Lever | Object it acts on | Stratum / dimension | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CE stage** | coarse partition (bulk interiors) | codim-0, high-eigenvalue dirs | bulk regions right; AdamW fine here |
| **τ/l7 softplus** | SDF margin temperature | engages codim-1 | "CE+softplus LOWER d_seg" — begin boundary refine |
| **β-anneal hosc 4→8 (FEED-fe)** | per-coordinate BASIS sharpness | codim-1 edge (representation/chart) | step-native L∞-at-edge, Gibbs-free; ⊥ optimizer |
| **Eikonal \|∇φ\|=1 (FEED-ew)** | field SLOPE / normal direction | codim-1 normal (output passband) | R-survival by construction (587×); slope, NOT placement |
| **MUON finisher** | optimizer step spectrum (placement) | codim-1 PLACEMENT + **biggest relative win at codim-2/3** | releases the starved low-energy boundary subspace |
| **LEVER-4 KKT waterfill (FEED-fg)** | code/film capacity allocation | codim-1 annulus × 3D temporal manifold | route rank-32 code to low-own-margin band |
| **φ_k priors (FEED-et/fd: lane-SDF/hood/sky)** | strata OFFLOAD (geometric+static) | codim-0 interiors + predictable lane curve + static hood | free the learned capacity for Lane+Movable residual |

**Coherence verdict: the stack is COHERENT and largely ORTHOGONAL-BY-CONSTRUCTION** — eikonal(slope) ⊥ Muon(placement) ⊥ β-anneal(basis) ⊥ LEVER-4(allocation) ⊥ φ_k-priors(strata) act on DIFFERENT mathematical objects, so they compose rather than conflict. Two findings:
- **SYNERGY (not just orthogonality) on `film`:** LEVER-4 concentrating code energy into few dims makes `film`'s input covariance MORE anisotropic → Muon's relative benefit on `film` GROWS. Muon×LEVER-4 are synergistic on the per-frame conditioning path.
- **THE ONE GAP (binding):** the **codim-2/3 junction conditioning is UN-covered by any dedicated lever.** Eikonal pins each |∇φ_k|=1 but does NOT constrain junction geometry (separatrix meeting angles / the power-diagram vertices). Muon only relieves GENERAL ill-conditioning there. A thin multi-component Movable region = a codim-2 medial-axis RIDGE where one φ must poke above two neighbors along a 1-D curve — exactly the FEED-ew "a single φ-field can't represent multi-component Movable" wall. This is a REPRESENTATIONAL hole in the K=5 power-diagram chart, and it is precisely where FEED-fh/ff parked the deferred witness-seeded residual-sharpener. The lattice is coherent; its single un-covered stratum is the codim-2/3 Movable junction. The dropped "smooth" stage is correctly excluded (it RAISES d_seg — keeping the partition sharp is coherent with everything above).

### (3) THROUGH-R SPECTRAL COMPATIBILITY — Muon RESPECTS the passband IFF on the realized-through-R loss + eikonal held (muon-lr / ns-steps regime)
R = bicubic↑(384→874)→uint8→bilinear↓(512×384) = a low-pass + resample with its own passband; FEED-ff: sharp-is-worse because |∇sine|≫1 aliases ringing into flips, cure = |∇m|~1.
- **KEY DISTINCTION (resolves the apparent tension): Muon conditions the WEIGHT-UPDATE spectrum (parameter space), NOT the OUTPUT-FIELD spectrum (image space).** The output spatial-frequency content is set by the BASIS (curvelet/Fourier freqs + hosc ω,β) and bounded by the EIKONAL slope — Muon injects NO high spatial frequency into the output. **So Muon is spectrally NEUTRAL on the output passband; it does not over-sharpen the boundary spectrally by itself.**
- **SECOND-ORDER tension (the real one):** by releasing the low-energy boundary directions, Muon fits the boundary more aggressively. If the LOSS were a FIELD-LEVEL margin proxy, that extra fitting power could drive the boundary sharper than R's passband → Gibbs returns through R (FEED-cn T=0.1 self-defeat). The PROTECTION is structural: the witness trains on **REALIZED d_seg THROUGH R (score-domain loss, FEED-ey)** — the gradient already PRE-DISTORTS the boundary to survive R. As long as Muon optimizes the SAME through-R realized objective, its faster boundary-fitting drives toward R-SURVIVAL placement, not field-sharpness. **VERDICT: Muon RESPECTS the R passband PROVIDED (a) the loss is realized-through-R and (b) eikonal stays ON during the finisher.** The tension only materializes if a Muon finisher is run on a field-level proxy — FORBIDDEN here.
- **Recommended regime (condition WITHOUT over-sharpening):** **`--muon-ns-steps 5` (do NOT change)** — ns_steps controls only the orthogonalization quality of the step itself (5 = Keller-Jordan's converged value; <3 under-orthogonalizes → reverts toward Adam-like; >5 = wasted compute, same fixed point, no spectral benefit). It is NOT an over-sharpening knob. **`--muon-lr 1e-3…2e-3` (the CONSERVATIVE end of FEED-fi's 1e-3…5e-3 range)** because: (i) the finisher runs FLAT (FEED-fi froze the cosine schedule) so a high flat LR accumulates; (ii) the unit-spectral-norm step makes even a modest LR move the boundary meaningfully; (iii) the finisher's job is REFINEMENT (placement), not bulk re-fit. **HOLD `--eikonal-weight` (do NOT drop it during the finisher)** so the output slope stays clamped to the R passband while Muon refines placement within it. momentum 0.95 / nesterov on (defaults). This is the eikonal-clamps-slope + Muon-refines-placement decomposition operationalized.

### (4) MORSE-SMALE SEPARATRIX × MUON — reaches the codim-1 budget; the Movable medial-axis REPRESENTATION binds first
The witness argmax IS a soft Morse-Smale complex; the separatrix = margin-zero set (FEED-fh AUC 0.9987); the binding residual ≈244 px witness-wrong (margin-gated). Sub-0.15 d_seg budget = **5.2–6.5e-4** (FEED-ew); measured n96 witness = **0.00124** (~2× the budget).
- **Muon DOES sharpen separatrix conditioning toward the budget on the codim-1 Lane long-tail** — it releases the low-energy boundary-PLACEMENT subspace AdamW starves, plausibly closing part of the ~2× gap (this is WHY it is the measured "THE drop" stage and the single most-potent OPTIMIZER lever). **But Muon improves placement of whatever the ARCHITECTURE CAN represent; it cannot make a single smooth `φ_Movable` field carve multiple disconnected medial-axis car-blobs that the K=5 power-diagram chart structurally cannot represent (the codim-2 ridge, FEED-ew/fh).** That is a REPRESENTATIONAL limit, not an optimization-conditioning limit — orthogonal to what Muon fixes.

### 0. The objective IS a Lagrangian (why this is a SOLVE not a sweep)
`S(θ) = 100·d_seg(θ) + √(10·d_pose) + 25·B(θ)/37,545,489`. The score weights {100, 1, 25} ARE the Lagrange multipliers — so the unconstrained `min_θ S` is exactly the RD **water-fill** (KKT stationarity `∂S/∂B = 0`). No constrained sweep needed: the math closes. Pose is off-witness (stored Quantizr sidecar, d_pose~3.4e-5 ⇒ `√(10·d_pose)=0.0184` ≈ const) → the witness's ONLY controllable terms are d_seg and B.

### 1. The response surfaces assembled (MEASURED / BORROWED / PREDICTED labels)
- **Byte model** `B(h,m) = 0.915·(88h + 8hm + 4h² + 8h) + 0.885·m·1200` [MEASURED FEED-eu; my repro: B(96,32)=98,634 vs measured 99,790 = **−1.16%**; ∂B/∂h=1028 B, ∂B/∂m=1765 B ⇒ **hidden is 1.72× cheaper per unit**]. - **RD curve** `d_seg(B)=d_ref·(B_a/B)^α` [d_ref=0.00124 MEASURED n96-converged hosc/l7 = OPTIMISTIC lower bound; CONS 0.0025 = 2× gen-gap; α∈{1.5 FEED-cq, 2.0 FEED-fk first-principles, 2.34 FEED-cc} BORROWED].
- **mod SVD eff-rank = 13.5, 90%-energy@21** [MEASURED FEED-fl] ⇒ mod=32 is 1.5× over-wide; fold to 21 d_seg-neutral (<10% energy).
- **directional all-class basis = ×0.52 d_seg, 0 bytes** [MEASURED −48%]. **Muon = "THE drop"** [PREDICTED ~6–9e-4 orthogonal, FEED-fk; NOT folded into the S band — upside margin].

## FEED-gc (2026-06-27 ~19:50 CDT) — level-set dashboard now SELF-FOLLOWING + STALENESS-HONEST (extincts "DEAD-run rendered as live")

**Bug class extincted:** `tools/render_levelset_dashboard.py` watched a STOPPED run's log for hours — the daemon kept running + refreshing the HTML while its data source was dead, so a fresh-looking dashboard silently showed stale numbers. NO-FAKE: a "live" dashboard over dead data is a fake-live claim.

**Fix (additive to the one tool; old `--log` behavior unchanged):**
1. **Self-follow** — new `--log-glob PATTERN` (default `.omx/tmp/levelset_*.log`). Each refresh cycle RE-RESOLVES the watched log to the NEWEST-mtime file matching the glob **that actually contains verdict lines**. The verdict-filter is load-bearing: the glob also matches the dashboard's OWN daemon log (`levelset_dashboard_daemon.log`, 0 verdicts, newest-mtime because it's rewritten every cycle) — without the filter the dashboard would self-follow its own log and fake "live" forever. New run starts (new log) → auto-switch (an `▶ following <basename> (switched <utc>)` line in the HTML). `--log` stays as explicit back-compat override (returned verbatim).
2. **Staleness banner keyed to the WATCHED LOG's real mtime** (verdict lines carry no timestamp — confirmed; mtime is the honest "still being written?" signal): `● live (updated Ns ago)` when fresh; a LOUD red `⚠ STALE — no new verdict in Nm — run may be STOPPED/crashed` when age > `--stale-min` (default 5). `⚠ no run log found` when the glob matches nothing. This is the honesty layer — fresh-HTML-over-dead-data is now impossible to miss.
3. All existing panels (d_seg/d_pose/blob_bytes/implied_S vs epoch, tau/l7 stage lines, goal-d_seg hline) + the `[macOS-MLX training] NON-PROMOTABLE · pointer UNMOVED 0.19110` footer + meta-refresh preserved.

## FEED-gf (2026-06-27 ~22:?? CDT) — level-set dashboard staleness is now SELF-CALIBRATING + honest (extincts the fixed-`--stale-min` false-alarm) + a bounded visual/self-explanatory upgrade; durable `ts` root-cause fix landed in the trainer

**Bug class extincted (telemetry accuracy is VITAL — operator: "accurate, or we understand+flag when it isn't"):** the dashboard's live/stale JUDGMENT keyed off the LOG FILE mtime against a hand-set fixed minute threshold. The trainer writes in CLUSTERS (`checkpoint`+`reorient`+`verdict`+`verdict_async_done`) roughly every 25 epochs; the async verdict itself takes ~200s (`verdict_async_done.secs` measured 199–312s); QUIET stretches BETWEEN clusters run 8–13+ min on a PERFECTLY HEALTHY run (verified live: a **488s / 8.1-min** quiet stretch at ep700 while pid 51464 was 27.5% CPU and descending). So the old `--stale-min 5` false-alarmed "STOPPED"; the band-aid `--stale-min 45` papered over it but would ALSO hide a real death for 45 min. A fixed minute band cannot be right across CE/tau/l7/Muon (different cadences). NO-FAKE: a confidently-wrong live/stale claim is a fake telemetry claim.

**Fix — DATA-DERIVED staleness (`tools/render_levelset_dashboard.py`, additive; `--log`/`--log-glob`/all panels preserved):**
1. **Self-observe the verdict cadence.** The dashboard records the wall-time when each NEW verdict EPOCH first appears, persisting a tiny per-log state file (`--cadence-state`, default `.omx/tmp/dash_levelset_cadence.json`, keyed by log NAME so calibration survives a dashboard restart but a NEW run starts fresh — never inherits a dead run's cadence). Epochs already present at launch are a BASELINE latched at "now" and EXCLUDED from measured inter-arrivals (they did not arrive on our clock). `cadence = MEDIAN inter-arrival of new verdict epochs`.
2. **STALE only when `verdict_age > max(floor, K × cadence)`** (K=2.5, floor=10 min) → auto-adapts to each stage's cadence. Before ≥3 measured arrivals the state is **`● warming up — calibrating cadence (prior ~18m, n/3 samples)`** (amber, NOT red, NOT a false STALE), using a LABELED prior; a process that died right after launch is still caught during warmup by a secondary `log_age > floor` guard.
3. **Two honest facts, never blurred:** `last verdict ep<N> (<Mm> ago)` [the d_seg recency — what matters] vs `log active <Ns> ago` [file mtime — process-writing proxy]; plus `next ~ep<N+spacing> (~<Mm>)` from the cadence (epoch spacing is data-derived = median epoch diff).
4. **`--stale-min` kept as an optional HARD FLOOR override** (back-compat): when set it replaces the self-calibrated floor in `max(floor, K×cadence)`; UNSET (new default) = fully self-calibrated. New args: `--stale-floor-min` (10), `--cadence-k` (2.5), `--cadence-prior-min` (18), `--cadence-state`.

**Visual / self-explanatory upgrade (bounded, NO JS/build/deps — single matplotlib→HTML page):** clean dark theme; big headline current-d_seg with ▼/▲ trend arrow + "N× the sub-0.19 goal"; plain-language status line ("de-confound witness · tau stage (tau_softplus) (→ l7@900) · l7 finisher at ep900, Muon after"); curriculum stage SHADING (CE/tau/l7+Muon) on the epoch axis + annotated tau/l7 lines; per-panel subtitles explaining each metric + what each goal/target hline means + that **implied_S is ADVISORY mid-training, NOT the contest score**; a one-line legend for the stage shading and the ●live / ●warming / ⚠stale meanings. `[macOS-MLX training] NON-PROMOTABLE · pointer UNMOVED 0.19110` footer + meta-refresh preserved.

**Durable root-cause fix (the no-timestamp cause):** added an ADDITIVE `"ts": <UTC>` field to the trainer's verdict log lines (`experiments/train_levelset_witness_realized_through_R_mlx.py`, all 3 emit sites: baseline + sync + async). Purely observational log metadata — NEVER read back into training, NOT appended to `history`/`result.json`, zero resume/parity impact (resume reads the npz); the RUNNING pid 51464 keeps its in-memory code so the live run is unaffected; py_compile OK. The dashboard reads `ts` DIRECTLY when present → FUTURE runs calibrate INSTANTLY (no warmup); the current ts-less run uses the self-observed path. Verified: embedded-`ts` → instant measured `● live`.

**Tests:** `experiments/tests/test_render_levelset_dashboard_self_follow.py` — **46 pass** (was 22). New: `_verdict_ts_epoch` parse/absent; `_epoch_spacing` median; `_arrival_times` embedded-ts-all-measured + self-observed-baseline-excluded; `_measure_cadence` becomes-measured-after-3-new-arrivals; `_compute_liveness` missing/warming/live-within-cadence/stale->2.5x/warmup-dead-caught-by-log-floor/embedded-ts-instant-live/verdict-age-distinct-from-log-age; `_cfg_from_args` default-floor + `--stale-min` hard-floor-override (live-vs-stale contrast); cadence-state roundtrip + per-log isolation; `_banner_html` 4 states + both recency facts; `_write_html` headline+legend present.

### FEED-gf CORRECTION (same session) — the first staleness cut FALSE-ALARMED on the live healthy run; FIXED to a simpler single-threshold model + a visual declutter (screenshot-verified)

**Bug in the first FEED-gf cut (caught by my own live-verify + corroborated by the operator/coordinator within minutes — telemetry accuracy IS vital):** the initial `warming_up` model used a separate dead-process guard `log_age > floor (10m)`, and a HEALTHY quiet stretch on THIS run reaches **~11-15 min** (operator-confirmed; observed live at 10.4m) → it cried **⚠ STALE on a live run** (pid 51464 at 30% CPU). (c) a HEALTHY run now reads **`● live`** (a calm amber **`◐ warming up`** pill ONLY while the cadence is still the prior — never the red STALE alarm); `⚠ stale` fires only when the last verdict is genuinely older than the (cadence-derived) threshold. ### THE REFRAME (measured, $0): the binding d_seg wall is NOT the contest R (render→bicubic↑874→uint8→bilinear↓384).
`L*` lives at 384 = scorer res, so R is a near-identity band-limited round-trip; at render res ≥384 EVERY boundary
rep — even naive single-channel PALETTE — survives R to d_seg<1e-4. The famous palette ×170-350 death is therefore
sub-wall (C) the FROZEN SegNet reading an off-distribution flat-color image, NOT the resample. Decomposition:
(A) resample/uint8 survival = BENIGN · (B) witness render-res / capacity = THE WALL · (C) SegNet RGB-reading = the
other half (trainer's realized-through-R `cpu_verdict_d_seg`).
### MEASURED capacity cliff (LANE class-1 flip% / total survival d_seg, n=96, identical R for all reps):
| render | palette lane% | hard lane% | **SDF lane%** | hard total | **SDF total** |
| 96  | 58.7 | 58.2 | 41.9 | 0.0160 | 0.0051 |
| 192 | 26.3 | 25.9 | **3.19** | 0.0063 | **0.00059** |
| 320 | 25.7 | 25.6 | **0.04** | 0.0062 | **0.00001** |
| 384 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | ~0 | 0 |
### THE MINIMAL R-INVARIANT REP = a WIDE-ramp 1-Lipschitz multi-class SDF (`argmax_k φ_k`): smooth (no bicubic
Gibbs), 1-Lipschitz margin (linear-through-zero → sub-pixel boundary), wide decision band (uint8 averages → sub-
precision placement). R's bicubic/bilinear is then a RECONSTRUCTION FILTER — sdf@192 survival 0.00059 < its own
nearest pre-R proxy 0.00555 (R actively HELPS the SDF). SDF buys ~2× render-res headroom: SDF@192 ≈ hard@384.
### SLOPE: wider ramp strictly better — @192 lane flip 10.3%(0.66px)→3.19%(2.6px)→2.95%(≥5.3px, saturates); sharp
SDF is 3.5× worse. Want margin-band half-width ≳5px (slope ≲24/px). LANE geom: median 2.0px, 76%≤2px, 0%≤1px, above
384-Nyquist (so survives at 384) → sub-Nyquist only once witness render res ≲192 (= the measured cliff).
### V2 SURVIVAL TERM: (1) SDF level-set carrier not hard/palette (substrate exists: lever_b_levelset_generator +
lane_sdf_component); (2) WIDE margin ramp (≳5px, add margin-band regularizer); (3) render ≥192 knee (≥320 for lane);
(4) LANE gets a dedicated MSDF-style multi-channel (dash CORNERS) — even SDF@192 leaves 3.19% lane (the ~8-dim
long-tail, localized to sub-wall B); (5) keep R in-loop; (6) DON'T spend bytes fighting R — spend on SDF effective
render-res (B) + SegNet-reading (C). OSS: Chlumský 2018 MSDF (SDF interp accurate only where |∇|~const; corners need
multi-channel) + coverage/area-AA (wide ramp = sub-pixel coverage) confirm the physics.

`r_survival_probe_scalespace_n48.json`): R's OWN kernel is tiny/benign (edge-spread eff σ ≈0.38px@384, 0.52px@874,
→1.2px@96; isolated thin bars survive R always). The "SDF survives because its level-set is heat-stable" claim is
FALSIFIED for a thin minority class: under the EXACT heat kernel (gaussian blur→argmax) the SDF does NOT beat hard

INTERP/R@192 SDF lane 3.19% (wins) — same rep, opposite ranking → R is INTERPOLATION-dominant, NOT diffusion-
dominant. Scale-space still gives the right Nyquist cliff (r≳192 for w=2px lane), but rep-survival ranking =
interpolation-exactness-on-linear-ramps, not heat-stability. v2 spec unchanged, now mechanistically grounded:
SDF wins BECAUSE R interpolates.

## FEED-wfs1 (2026-07-02): WAVE-F Stage-1 OPTIMAL lane-band RD codec LANDED + MEASURED (n600 3.76x rate, decode-consistent)

**WHAT (means, RATE ENABLER — pointer 0.19110 UNMOVED):** replaced the Wave-E NAIVE per-pair lane serializer (each pair independent, float64 coeffs, brotli = 156,340 B @ n600, rate_term 0.1041 = launch-UNUSABLE vs a 0.19110 frontier) with the OPTIMAL **LBND2 rate-distortion codec** INSIDE the existing LVLS1 byte-close 5th-block grammar (R2's "build from scratch" was a grep false-negative on magic `LBND`; the real byte-close magic is `LVLS1` — I EXTENDED the Wave-E block). Commits `bae0283bf` (codec) + `305de5df?`→`305de5d` (byte-close wire-in + inflate `_lane_parse_rd`) + `dc64a9e81` (measured) + `10b137821` (results memo). Ledgers: `.omx/research/wave_f_lane_band_rd_code_LANDED_stage1_measured_20260702.md` + `.omx/research/wave_f_lane_band_rd_rate_n600_measured.json`.

**The codec (deep math):** **L4** lateral-sort ragged lines into fixed slots (ego-lane + offsets) + carry-forward hold for absent slots → **L3** quantize each coeff to its OWN geometric-tolerance step (centerline per-power scaled by `f_ref`, ~sub-px lateral) → **L2** temporal-delta across the 600 pairs → zigzag int32 → outer brotli (the entropy backend). Bit-exact + decode-consistent BY CONSTRUCTION (both sides render the DEQUANTIZED lines).

**MEASURED (n600, real `gt_n600.npz` lstars, byte-closed serialization, `[macOS-CPU advisory]` NON-PROMOTABLE, NEVER MPS):**
- naive LBND1 **156,340 B / rate 0.1041** → RD LBND2 **41,526 B / rate 0.02765** = **3.76× less** (ratio 0.2656), decode-consistent.
- delta-stream **Shannon floor = 26,179 B / rate 0.01743** → EVEN a PERFECT entropy coder on the camera-frame per-pair coeffs CANNOT cross the +0.005 rate floor (7,509 B): the residual is **INFORMATION-bound, not coding-bound** (→ the next lever is a SOURCE re-parameterization, FEED-unifiedxi, NOT a better coder).
- **PTC1 / constriction range-coder DOMINATED** (43,153 B > brotli 41,526 B: the per-dim transmitted-PMF header cost swamps the coded stream) → **brotli on zigzag-int32 is the correct backend** (KILLS the "add a range coder" gold-plating + keeps inflate dep-free). ## FEED-permlaw (2026-07-02): the UNIFYING LAW — an index-permutation discontinuity defeats every temporal model (correspondence MUST precede any temporal coder)

**WHAT (DERIVED law, means — pointer 0.19110 UNMOVED):** ONE principle explains BOTH measured failures (FEED-wfxi2). The LBND2 lateral-sort assigns slot *k* to the *k*-th lane BY LATERAL POSITION AT THAT FRAME; at a lane cross/birth/death the sort flips → the coefficient time-series OF A SLOT has a **discontinuity corresponding to NO physical motion** (a Morse-Smale separatrix-reconnection / saddle-swap event → composes with the persistence component `122e59ba8`). A PREDICTOR (LBND3, RVLD-style causal warp) codes swap-innovations = huge bytes (why LBND3 measured WORSE); a linear SMOOTHER averages across the swap into a phantom intermediate lane (why moving-average is LOSSY + can SPILL d_seg); a TRANSFORM (DCT/KLT) Gibbs-spreads the discontinuity across all frequencies. **MEASURED: 44% of the temporal-delta L1 mass sits in the top-5% largest jumps = the swap/outlier signature.** Therefore the correct ORDER is CORRESPONDENCE → (smooth/transform/predict), NEVER the reverse. SOTA video-lane-detection independently validates: RVLD (ICCV'23, causal one-frame warp ≈ our failed LBND3) → LaneTCA (2024, longer-window batch aggregation, higher F1) = batch BEATS causal-one-step, exactly our LBND3-vs-smoothing result. Ledger `.omx/research/lane_coeff_tracking_denoising_optimal_survey_20260702.md` (ON-WORKTREE).

**TRIALITY sync:** DAG (this FEED-permlaw) ↔ **equation** `index_permutation_discontinuity_defeats_temporal_model_v1` REGISTERED (2 MEASURED anchors = 0.44 top-5% swap mass + the both-failures-explained row, VERIFIED_VIA_EMPIRICAL_ANCHOR residual 0.0; callable `top5pct_jump_mass_fraction()`) ↔ **DSL** the `LaneGauge` correspondence-first pipeline note ENCODES the law (correspondence-first ORDER; DESIGN-STAGE #234). **HARD GATE: pointer 0.19110 UNMOVED** — the 0.44 swap mass is MEASURED; the law is DERIVED (explains both measured failures + SOTA-validated).
